content.user_title: Build a specification-driven Claude Code workflow
content.value_statement: Projects can lose alignment when requirements, prompts, and implementation evolve separately. This skill provides a structured workflow that keeps specifications and Claude Code work connected through each development phase.
actual_capabilities: Defines a specification-first workflow for planning, implementation, review, and refinement.
Guides repository-wide and folder-specific CLAUDE.md guidance.
Recommends formats, naming conventions, and quality checks for specification files.
Connects implementation tasks to specification requirements and acceptance criteria.
Supports iterative prompt refinement using documented feedback and successful patterns.
Outlines quality checks for specifications, implementation work, and team workflow consistency.
limitations: It provides conceptual guidance and does not create files, run commands, or validate code automatically.
It assumes the project already has a repository structure and clear requirements.
It does not replace project-specific architecture, security, or testing decisions.
Teams that prefer unstructured or code-first work may not benefit from this workflow.

use_cases.title: Start a feature with clear acceptance criteria
use_cases.description: Turn feature requirements into a specification-first plan before asking an AI coding assistant to implement the work.

use_cases.title: Standardize a multi-folder repository
use_cases.description: Define root and folder-specific CLAUDE.md guidance so teams use consistent conventions across a repository.

use_cases.title: Improve AI-assisted delivery practices
use_cases.description: Create a repeatable loop for reviewing prompts, comparing results with specifications, and documenting lessons learned.

prompt_templates.title: Create a simple feature workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me create a specification-first workflow for a new feature. Ask for the goal, acceptance criteria, repository area, and validation steps before proposing an implementation plan.

prompt_templates.title: Review specification completeness
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this feature specification for clarity, testability, edge cases, and acceptance criteria. List missing decisions and propose concise questions for stakeholders.

prompt_templates.title: Design repository guidance
prompt_templates.prompt: Based on this repository structure and team conventions, propose root and folder-specific CLAUDE.md responsibilities. Avoid duplicating rules and identify where overrides are needed.

prompt_templates.title: Run a traceability review
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare the implementation plan, specification, and acceptance criteria for this feature. Produce a traceability matrix, identify gaps, and recommend the next validation actions.

output_examples.input: Plan a user profile editing feature with validation and audit requirements.
output: A feature specification with user flows, validation rules, and acceptance criteria.
An implementation sequence mapped to the specification sections.
A validation checklist covering errors, permissions, and audit records.

output_examples.input: Create guidance for a repository with frontend, API, and shared library folders.
output: Repository-wide conventions for the root guidance file.
A review process for keeping specifications and implementation guidance current.

best_practices: Write measurable acceptance criteria before implementation begins.
Keep repository guidance concise and place specialized rules near the relevant folder.
Review implementation results against the specification at regular checkpoints.
anti_patterns: Starting implementation with ambiguous requirements or no success criteria.
Duplicating conflicting guidance across root and folder-specific instruction files.
Treating AI-generated output as complete without specification and quality review.

faq.question: What does this skill provide?
faq.answer: It provides conceptual guidance for a specification-driven workflow using Spec-Kit and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does this skill modify my repository?
faq.answer: No. It describes a workflow and does not create, edit, or execute files.

faq.question: Who should use this skill?
faq.answer: Developers and teams that want clearer requirements and more consistent AI-assisted implementation work.

faq.question: Can I use it for an existing project?
faq.answer: Yes. Start by documenting the current structure, conventions, and relevant specifications.

faq.question: Does it replace testing or security review?
faq.answer: No. Use project-specific testing, security review, and release processes in addition to this workflow.

faq.question: Is Spec-Kit required?
faq.answer: The guidance is designed for Spec-Kit concepts, but the workflow can inform other structured specification practices.
